name: Custom Snare Drum
shortDescription: High-tension 14-inch cylindrical membranophone featuring coiled steel snares and dual tensioned heads.
description: The snare drum produces a sharp, staccato crack created by striking the upper batter head, which causes rapid internal air compression that forces the lower resonant head to rattle against coiled steel snare wires.
historicalOrigins: Descended from the medieval tabor and Renaissance Swiss military field drums used for marching cadences.
acousticPrinciples: Circular membrane eigenmodes governed by Bessel functions Jm(kr): non-integer harmonic overtones (1.0 : 1.59 : 2.14 : 2.30)
Cavity coupling: Air trapped inside the drum cylinder acts as an acoustic spring coupling the top and bottom heads
Snare rattle: High-frequency chaos noise burst (~2 kHz – 10 kHz) generated by non-linear impact of steel coils

characteristics.pitchRange: Indefinite pitch center (~180 Hz – 350 Hz depending on tension tuning)
characteristics.timbralColor: Snappy, explosive, bright, transient-heavy, biting crack
characteristics.orchestralRole: Rhythmic pulse, backbeat engine, military roll, dynamic accentuation

soundDNA.exciter: Drumstick tip or brush striking the coated batter head
soundDNA.resonator: 10-ply American Maple cylinder shell with 45° bearing edges
soundDNA.harmonics: Inharmonic Bessel circular membrane modes with wideband snare noise
soundDNA.attackDecay: Ultra-fast attack (< 1ms) with immediate snappy decay (0.2s–0.8s)
soundDNA.timbreProfile: Dry punchy fundamental with sizzling high-frequency snare buzz
soundDNA.radiationPattern: Dipole-like radiation from top and bottom heads with lateral shell vibration

drum_shell.label: 10-Ply Maple Shell
drum_shell.function: Forms resonant acoustic cylinder cavity and supports structural tension of hoops.

characteristics.material: 10-ply North American Rock Maple with hand-rubbed nitrocellulose lacquer
characteristics.mechanism: Acoustic cylinder chamber and bearing edge contact

membrane_top.label: Batter Head (Top Membrane)
membrane_top.function: Impact reception surface; undergoes radial and circular transverse wave displacement.

membrane_bottom.label: Snare Side Head (Bottom Membrane)
membrane_bottom.function: Ultra-thin membrane that vibrates sympathetically with top head to activate snare wires.

hoops.label: Die-Cast Steel Hoops
hoops.function: Clamps drumheads securely against bearing edges with even perimeter distribution.

tension_rods.label: Tension Rods & Lugs
tension_rods.function: Precision threaded bolts allowing micro-tuning of drumhead tension around perimeter.

characteristics.material: Stainless steel 7/32-inch bolts with brass swivel nuts

snare_wires.label: Coiled Steel Snare Wires
snare_wires.function: 20-strand steel coils that bounce violently against resonant head producing signature sizzle.

characteristics.material: High-carbon coiled steel wires soldered to bronze end plates
characteristics.mechanism: Nonlinear impact vibration and chaotic boundary collision

followTheSound.title: Stick Strike & Impact
followTheSound.explanation: A wooden drumstick strikes the batter head, transferring kinetic energy and deforming the membrane downward.

followTheSound.title: Internal Air Pressure Wave
followTheSound.explanation: The batter head displacement compresses internal air within the shell, propagating an acoustic compression wave downwards.

followTheSound.title: Bottom Head Sympathy
followTheSound.explanation: The compressed air column pushes the thin resonant head outward, flexing it in microsecond sympathy.

followTheSound.title: Snare Wire Collision
followTheSound.explanation: The rebounding bottom head strikes the tensioned steel coils, generating high-frequency chaotic rattling noise.

followTheSound.title: Acoustic Radiation & Rimshot
followTheSound.explanation: The combined inharmonic membrane thud and metallic snare crack radiate outward in an explosive acoustic wavefront.
